title: Locality-driven slot binning and soft-thaw policy for paged KV cache
creator: Marcus Li
description: Problem: Under mixed customer workloads we see high KV cache churn leading to prefill misses and decode CPU spikes. Current slab/slot allocator evicts by simple LRU within segments which creates oscillation when request locality shifts (e.g., conversational bursts followed by background batch runs). This ticket prototypes a locality-driven slot binning allocator and a 'soft-thaw' residency policy to reduce thrash and enable low-latency prefill hits for short-lived hot contexts. Approach: 1) Maintain lightweight per-tenant 'slot bins' based on recent access locality (conversation-id or shard fingerprint). Bins provide soft affinity for pages so related fragments are co-located and prefer the same decode worker. 2) Implement soft-thaw: recently-evicted pages enter a thawable stand-by state (small compressed footprint) for a configurable time window before full reclamation. If a reaccess occurs during the window we rehydrate in-place avoiding a full decode. 3) Add deferred decode handoff: when a prefill miss is predicted but latency SLO allows, schedule decode to a background decode worker pool and pre-reserve a slot, reducing critical-path contention on the real-time decode path. 4) Integrate an eviction simulator that models slot bins, thaw windows, and background decode throughput to tune thresholds. Success metrics: increase prefill hit rate by +8-12% on mixed workloads, reduce decode CPU tail by 20%, and keep P99 generation latency delta <= +5ms for real-time requests.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype slot-binning allocator integrated into paged-KV layer behind feature flag
Soft-thaw lifecycle implemented with configurable window and memory accounting
Deferred decode handoff implemented with metrics for handoff latency and success rate
Eviction simulator runs for representative workload traces and produces tuning recommendations
No regression: P95 latency for tenant baseline workloads not increased by more than 3%
Documentation for new knobs (bin-size, thaw-window, handoff-threshold) added to runtime config docs
updates: 2025-02-12: Triage and spec drafted after spike with infra team. Decided to prioritize soft-thaw + binning over full segment rearchitecture to reduce surface area.
2025-02-18: Spike prototype (in-memory only) shows simulated 10% prefill hit increase on conv-burst trace. Attached simulator config and traces in Confluence.

2025-02-22: Design review with PM and SRE. Concerns raised about memory accounting for thawed pages and worst-case footprint. Agreed on explicit soft-cap per-GPU node and admission control for thawed state.
2025-02-26: Implemented basic slot bin metadata and thaw-state marker in paged-kv store. Added unit tests for lifecycle transitions.

2025-03-01: Run simulator with background decode pool model (1:4 decode:rt-worker) showing decode CPU tail reduction ~18% for mixed trace. P99 impact on latency for real-time requests simulated at +3ms.

2025-03-02: Engineering review feedback (see PR #6124): need to add telemetry for thawed-rescue-rate and explicit evicted-by-policy tags. Blocking: GPU infra team needs quota to run canary in dedicated cluster. Next: add memory hard-limits and integrate with residency scheduler (ENG-61234).
